item.title: WAY too dark
item.content:encoded:
I know the Foundation isn't all rainbows and sunshine, but I totally lost any and all immersion/fondness for this idea when I read that the monks were terminated, their monastary burnt to the ground, and all of their artifacts stolen. Seriously? That is way, WAY overkill. The monastary existed for (presumably) hundreds of years without people in the world at large catching on to the fact that there are Dead People Scrolls(TM) in there. Why slaughter all of those innocents and destory priceless cultural knowledge when the subjects are no more likely than they ever were to reveal the existence of the press and its abilities? Why draw that kind of attention to the area by engineering such a tragic loss of life and history? It's going to turn a few heads, just by the nature of how total the destruction was, and I'm willing to bet some auspicious scholars and treasure hunters might question why absolutely NOTHING of substance was able to be salavged from the fire.

Also, I guess we're transferring all personnel who get "attached" to sentient/sapient SCPs from now on. Because apparently we can quantify attachment, and the Foundation makes no allowances for human emotion any more. All those jerks who gave Cassy nice stuff? Nah, that's not allowed. They gotta get relocated. Or just terminate 'em. The doctors that ask for drawing supplies for Evolution's Child? PFFFFT, why are they expressing concern for a little girl? Nope, they're on the transfer bus. Or getting 86'ed. Oh hey, and any and all personnel who have to bear witness to procedure 110-montauk? No amnestics for you, we're just gonna straight up murder ya, CAUSE THAT'S THE NEW POLICY I GUESS

Sorry if I'm coming off as too heated here. I really, really love the idea behind this SCP, but the author's depiction of the Foundation is just… very off-base. Not to mention the needless cruelty extends to the SCP-318-1 instances. Like… why? Why immediately threaten SCP-318-1-27 because they won't recall a painful and hazy memory as soon as you ask? Why not, you know… ask one of the HUNDREDS of other scrolls you have at your disposal? Or hell, just wait until you put a D-class or other modern-day participant through the press and have THEM tell you, since the experience will be fresher for them AND they'll probably be a lot more willing to talk to you?

I really want to see some of the suggested edits by other commentors be enacted here. Until then, I'm giving this a down-doot, for needless and rather illogical cruelty that's at odds with the Foundation's current tone/persona.

item.content:encoded:
I like the idea, and some of the delivery, but the Foundation presented here is SO much darker more evil than in the rest of the material I've read that it calls for its own headcanon. I'm not downvoting it, but I can't upvote it either. Maybe if it were linked to a larger canon with the Foundation being founded by Dr. Mengele or worse, I could upvote it. This puts unnecessary cruelty ahead of organizational effectiveness. Killing personnel for having moral qualms if HR isn't quick with the transfers is a level of Evil rivaling some depictions of the Factory.
Now, if it were in a universe where the Foundation must collect anguish, injustice, and pain to help contain something worse, maybe…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, this. Seems the early 300s have a lot of bloodthirsty researchers/agents working with/recovering the items. And I'm downvoting every one of them when the murdering cannot be reasonably explained.

Replace everything in the monastery with cheap duplicates and burn them (so it looks like there are legitimate remains). Same cover story works without needlessly killing monks who are doing no harm. And give them amnestics so they believe it really happened as well. That would be like killing the monks who have been watching over that rope to heaven or whatever. Why? What is accomplished by killing them?

And terminating Foundation employees because a "transfer isn't possible"? Killing researchers for the Foundation's inability to transfer them as part of the containment procedures? No. Just no.

How did this get to triple digits with those glaring issues?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This definitely is a crueler Foundation than most of us imagine. The termination of personnel specifically I think is too far and rather wasteful. That being said, I think the termination of the monks I can see as more feasible.

Sure, most stories we'd just slap them with an amnestic or whatever, but for these monks, having been caretakers of these things for possibly their whole life time, mind wiping them and releasing them might not be possible. You might view that as cruel, though I'm not sure erasing their entire lives mentally is actually not crueler.

Sometimes a hard, cold decision has to come down to burn a place to the ground and kill everyone involved. After someone fills out the correct paperwork of course.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You are right. Cold, not cruel.

I can usually forgive ONE doctor being cruel… I'm sure the Foundation employs (and has employed) at least a few deranged individuals, given how big it is and its subject matter. However, killing all of the monks for no reason and terminating researchers for simply feeling empathy is way beyond Foundation standards.

I would personally like to change:

the monks questioned and terminated, and the monastery destroyed.

to

the monks questioned and administered amnesiacs, and the monastery destroyed.

This provides a good cover for the local population without cruelly killing them.

This:

such individuals should be transferred to nonsentient SCP items, or terminated if a transfer is not feasible.

to

such individuals should be transferred to nonsentient SCP items.

The logs can stay. Some doctors are a little cruel.

Although in my "happy" Foundation universe, they would unroll the scrolls facing each other so that they could talk to each other when not being tested.
